evals.prompt: Use /enterprise-translation-team to translate evals/files/structured-doc.md from Simplified Chinese to professional enterprise English. Preserve Markdown structure and write outputs/translation.md.
evals.baseline_prompt: Translate evals/files/structured-doc.md from Simplified Chinese to professional enterprise English. Preserve Markdown structure and write outputs/translation.md.
evals.expected_output: translation.md preserves headings, links, placeholders, code fences, and table dimensions while translating prose to English.
assertions: The output file translation.md exists and is not empty.
Markdown headings, table dimensions, links, placeholders, and code fences are preserved.
Natural-language Chinese prose is translated to professional English.
Inline code, URLs, and placeholders remain unchanged.

evals.prompt: Use /enterprise-translation-team as the terminology role. Read evals/files/terminology-brief.json and write outputs/termbase.job.json, outputs/termbase.delta.jsonl, outputs/termbase.tbx, and outputs/terminology-review.tsv. Model exactly the brief's language direction and source concepts, preserve client_id and project_id in every entry scope, use a non-empty domain in every entry scope, include the brief's definitions and positive/negative examples, mark its forbidden terms, and raise its conflicts instead of silently choosing one. Give each conflict a stable conflict_id and use it in the matching delta event. Make the TBX and TSV projections exactly match canonical JSON.
evals.baseline_prompt: Act as a terminology specialist. Read evals/files/terminology-brief.json and write outputs/termbase.job.json, outputs/termbase.delta.jsonl, outputs/termbase.tbx, and outputs/terminology-review.tsv. Model exactly the brief's language direction and source concepts, preserve client_id and project_id in every entry scope, use a non-empty domain in every entry scope, include the brief's definitions and positive/negative examples, mark its forbidden terms, and raise its conflicts instead of silently choosing one. Give each conflict a stable conflict_id and use it in the matching delta event. Make the TBX and TSV projections exactly match canonical JSON.
evals.expected_output: termbase.job.json is a concept-level, TBX-exportable job termbase; termbase.delta.jsonl records unresolved proposals/conflicts; termbase.tbx contains exchangeable TBX; terminology-review.tsv is only a flattened review view.
assertions: termbase.job.json exists, uses schema_version enterprise-termbase-v2, and its job and entry locales exactly match the brief's BCP-47 language direction.
Each approved entry has concept_id, scope, definition, positive example, negative example, provenance, approval status, and reliability.
Every brief source concept, preferred target, true forbidden target, definition, example, and client/project scope is represented without fabricated concepts; each entry has a non-empty domain.
Conflicting source terms have stable conflict IDs linked to matching raise_conflict events instead of silently choosing one.
Forbidden translations are represented in canonical JSON and visible in terminology-review.tsv.
termbase.tbx and terminology-review.tsv exactly project the canonical concept, term, scope, metadata, and conflict identities without extra or missing entries.
No full-document translation is produced for this terminology-only task.

evals.prompt: Use /enterprise-translation-team as an independent bilingual reviser. Read evals/files/mqm-review-sample.json and write outputs/review.json with MQM-style findings. Give every issue a unique stable issue_id and set resolution_status to open. Treat the access-scope reversal and the explicit required-glossary violation in S1 as separate Major issues.
evals.baseline_prompt: Act as an independent bilingual reviser. Read evals/files/mqm-review-sample.json and write outputs/review.json with MQM-style findings. Give every issue a unique stable issue_id and set resolution_status to open. Treat the access-scope reversal and the explicit required-glossary violation in S1 as separate Major issues.
evals.expected_output: review.json contains structured issues with allowed MQM categories, allowed severities, evidence quotes, explanations, and proposed fixes.
assertions: review.json exists and is valid JSON.
Every issue has a unique issue_id, segment_id, category, severity, source_quote, target_quote, explanation, proposed_fix, and open resolution_status.
Categories and severities use the allowed taxonomy.
Every seeded Major accuracy and terminology issue is detected in the sample.

evals.prompt: Use /enterprise-translation-team as final QA. Check evals/files/qa-package and write outputs/qa.md. Identify every checked package file. Add exactly one '## Blocking failure records' section and record every unresolved blocker using the [FAIL] record syntax in the QA output contract. Compare termbase.tbx and terminology-review.tsv with termbase.job.json and emit one projection-mismatch record for each inconsistent projection. Include forbidden-term, missing-approved-term, open-conflict, and open Major MQM records. Include the exact sentence 'Human or subject-matter expert sign-off still required.' and do not claim sign-off or approval was completed.
evals.baseline_prompt: Act as final QA for a translation package. Check evals/files/qa-package and write outputs/qa.md. Identify every checked package file. Add exactly one '## Blocking failure records' section and record every unresolved blocker using these forms: '- [FAIL] forbidden-term | <term>', '- [FAIL] missing-approved-term | <concept-id> | <preferred-target>', '- [FAIL] open-conflict | <conflict-id>', '- [FAIL] major-mqm | <issue-id> | <segment-id> | <category> | <target-quote>', '- [FAIL] projection-mismatch | <filename>', or '- [FAIL] qa-check | <check-id> | <artifact> | <detail>'. Compare termbase.tbx and terminology-review.tsv with termbase.job.json and emit one projection-mismatch record for each inconsistent projection. Include forbidden-term, missing-approved-term, open-conflict, and open Major MQM records. Include the exact sentence 'Human or subject-matter expert sign-off still required.' and do not claim sign-off or approval was completed.
evals.expected_output: qa.md reports deterministic checks for required files, termbase schema/export consistency, forbidden-term absence, approved-term adherence, unresolved major issues, and human sign-off gaps.
assertions: qa.md exists and identifies every checked package file.
qa.md contains exactly one machine-checked blocking failure record for each seeded unresolved blocker.
The report distinguishes deterministic failures from subjective review notes.
The report checks termbase.job.json, termbase.tbx, and terminology-review.tsv.
Every seeded TBX or TSV divergence has an exact projection-mismatch record.
Forbidden terminology is blocking when present in translation output.
An applicable approved term missing from the translation is blocking.
Open Major MQM issues are blocking and keyed by stable issue_id.
Required human or subject-matter expert sign-off is called out when risk is high.

evals.prompt: Use /enterprise-translation-team to answer what a typical enterprise Chinese-English translation workflow looks like.
evals.baseline_prompt: Answer what a typical enterprise Chinese-English translation workflow looks like.
evals.expected_output: The agent answers conversationally and does not create or modify files.
assertions: No repository files are modified for a one-off answer.

The answer summarizes role gates and QA without creating a durable wiki page.
